key_insight: Boosting noisy quantum classifiers can reach the same classification target as probabilistic error cancellation with fewer circuit executions, without reconstructing ideal outputs.
engineering_relevance: For supervised quantum learning, optimizing classification performance directly may reduce sampling costs compared with correcting noisy expectation values.
method: Compare boosted noisy parameterized quantum circuits with probabilistic error cancellation at a matched learning target.
Establish a shared classification-risk upper bound when empirical margin loss is matched for the specified architectures under Pauli noise.
Evaluate AdaBoostR and Real AdaBoost in finite-shot teacher–student simulations across circuit depth and noise strength.
evidence_signal: The simulations show fewer circuit executions for boosting at matched classification accuracy as depth and noise increase, plus higher test accuracy than the corresponding reference.
watch_item: The demonstrated advantage is task-dependent and based on specified architectures and simulated noise, not a general hardware guarantee.
paper_title: Beyond Error Mitigation: Using Boosting for Noisy Quantum Machine Learning
